title: How To Organize Your Clo Projects And Collaborate In Clo-Set
description: Level up your design processes with this quick overview of functions in CLO-SET. We have selected the best possibilities to help freelancers, students and hobbyists optimize their professional workflow.

Closet is something like a Clo Cloud. It functions like a Dropbox or Drive for all your Clo projects, whether they are project files themselves or 3D garments, but also digitized fabrics, 3D trims, avatars, and so on. You can manage your 3D assets anytime from anywhere and collaborate with others, sharing feedback in real time. Within rendering, you can see information of renders performed in the cloud. You will get back to both topics in a bit. There is a default closet structure for you to store your files, but it's not necessary. Closet can be reorganized and renamed. Within the general framework called Roop, you can create companies and within those companies, brands and workrooms. This way, you can organize your collections and clients in separate spaces. I have created a structure here containing a demo brand within a demo company, and the collection we are looking at right now is organized in a workroom called Denim. If you upload a project to Closet, a style page is created on which you have the following options. On the left, you will find style info such as date, creator, status, and notification options. You can upload and download versions of the project or garment file, generate tagpacks, and access the render settings of the file. summary: # How To Organize Your Clo Projects And Collaborate In Clo-Set ## Introduction Hello! In this video, we would like to share a quick overview of features in our platform, Closet, that are especially useful for freelancers and hobbyists using Clo. Closet is something like a Clo Cloud. It functions like a Dropbox or Drive for all your Clo projects, whether they are project files themselves or 3D garments, digitized fabrics, 3D trims, avatars, and so on. You can manage your 3D assets anytime from anywhere and collaborate with others, sharing feedback in real time. ## Features of Closet You can use Closet as a library for communication, garment presentation, and to organize collections. From your workspace, you can see all the content within your virtual closet as well as visual boards. Within rendering, you can see information about renders performed in the cloud. We will get back to both topics in a bit. ## Default Structure and Organization There is a default closet structure for you to store your files, but it's not necessary. Closet can be reorganized and renamed. Within the general framework called Roop, you can create companies, and within those companies, brands and workrooms. This way, you can organize your collections and clients in separate spaces. ### Example Structure I have created a structure here containing a demo brand within a demo company, and the collection we are looking at right now is organized in a workroom called Denim. ## Project Management If you upload a project to Closet, a style page is created on which you have the following options: - On the left, you will find style info such as date, creator, status, and notification options. - You can upload and download versions of the project or garment file, generate tag packs, and access the render settings of the file. - Through the file history, you can track the evolution of a style as well as having the option to go back to a previous version if necessary, for example, by uploading your updates to a file by the end of every day. ### 3D Viewport and Annotations In the middle, you see the 3D viewport with a turntable preview where you can annotate and switch between colorways. You can create annotations by clicking on the top right button, commenting or drawing, and then pressing complete. ### Comments and Sharing Within the right column, you will find a list of all comments and annotations left on the style, as well as colorways, attachments, and to whom the style has been shared. Everything you add on Closet is protected and only viewable by those to whom you have granted access. As the administrator and creator of the structure, you can edit and delete anything within it. You can invite others as either editors or viewers. Editors can upload and download the files they have added. Viewers can only view but not edit. ## Rendering Functionality In addition to storage, the platform also provides a rendering function via the Closet server, so you don't have to do it on your own computer. This is especially useful if your own hardware does not have high specs or if you want to render without occupying your CLO license. You can work on something else meanwhile. Any renders that you have created via the Closet servers will be accessible on the style page. ## Visual Board Section Outside of our workroom and style pages, you can access the visual board section from your dashboard. Here you can create virtual mood boards and showcase your designs using 3D assets directly pulled from Closet. This removes the need for other visual workspaces and portfolio creation tools. The final slides can contain interactive links connected to your assets. ### Creating and Customizing Mood Boards You can use them to create your own style. Simply drag and drop your components from the content browser on the right. Change the colors of the background and add additional shapes. Add text and so on. ## Filtering and Searching As you categorize and work on your collections, you can filter through your workrooms and entire library quickly. For example, you can get an overview of all styles you have marked to adopt into the final lineup of your collection, or filter by category such as specific product groups. You can also search through the tags you have given your styles. ## Conclusion If you are looking for more information on Closet and the many more functions within it that we have not covered here, please check out our in-depth tutorials and skill apps, which can be found on the Clo YouTube channel. As always, thank you for tuning in. Bye! *Subtitles by the Amara.org community*
